description: Third synthetic workspace, held-out only: an engineering team's project memory in the shape agents actually write through remember (task-style subjects, long multi-clause objects), so the bar is also tested on dense facts rather than short attribute values. Fictional company, no real user data.

facts.subject: billing-webhook-retries task
facts.object: Webhook deliveries to customer endpoints retry with exponential backoff (30 seconds, 2 minutes, 10 minutes, 1 hour, 6 hours) for at most 24 hours; after that the event is marked dead and surfaced in the dashboard. Retries are idempotent through the delivery id, and a 410 response permanently disables the endpoint.

facts.subject: search-index-rebuild task
facts.object: The nightly rebuild doubled in duration because every shard was re-embedded even when its content hash was unchanged. Fix direction: skip unchanged shards using the stored content hash and re-embed only the delta. Measured on 1,000 shards: 41 minutes before, 6 minutes after.

facts.subject: auth-session-expiry task
facts.object: Sessions were expiring after 15 minutes of inactivity instead of 24 hours because the refresh cookie was set without Max-Age. Fixed and verified in staging on 2026-09-21; follow-up: add a regression test that asserts the cookie lifetime.

facts.subject: mobile-offline-sync task
facts.object: Offline sync ships for notes only in v1; attachments and comments are deferred to v2 because conflict resolution for binary files needs its own design. Conflicts on notes use last-writer-wins with a visible 'edited elsewhere' marker.

facts.subject: customer-export task
facts.object: Blocked on legal review of the export format; engineering work is complete and sits behind a feature flag named export_v2.

facts.subject: customer-export task
facts.object: Dana Whitfield

facts.subject: feature-flags
facts.object: Flags are snake_case, prefixed with the owning team, and removed within two releases after full rollout, for example growth_new_onboarding.

facts.subject: incident-2026-09-02
facts.object: Checkout returned 502 for 14 minutes after a bad config push to the edge proxy. Rolled back by reverting the config; detection came from a synthetic monitor, not from customers.

facts.subject: release-process
facts.object: Code freeze starts Wednesday 12:00 UTC before a Friday release; only fixes labelled release-blocker may merge during the freeze.

facts.subject: database-migrations
facts.object: Migrations must be backwards compatible with the previous release, so every schema change ships in two steps: add first, remove one release later. Never rename a column in place.

facts.subject: observability
facts.object: Application logs are kept for 30 days in hot storage and 12 months in cold storage; audit logs are kept for 7 years.

facts.subject: api-rate-limits
facts.object: Free tier: 60 requests per minute; paid tier: 600 requests per minute; bursts up to twice the limit for ten seconds.

facts.subject: onboarding-experiment
facts.object: The shorter three-step onboarding lifted activation from 41 percent to 47 percent over two weeks with 9,000 users per arm; the change shipped to 100 percent of users on 2026-09-18.

facts.subject: team-ritual
facts.object: Retrospective every second Friday at 15:00, rotating facilitator, action items tracked in the team wiki.

facts.subject: vendor-pdf-renderer
facts.object: Chose the self-hosted renderer over the SaaS API because per-document pricing would exceed 4,000 dollars a month at projected volume and because customer documents must not leave our network.

facts.subject: payments-provider-migration
facts.object: Cutover planned for 2026-11-04 with a two week dual-write period beforehand.

facts.subject: oncall
facts.object: Page the primary first; if there is no acknowledgement within 10 minutes page the secondary; after 20 minutes page the engineering manager.

facts.subject: dev-environment
facts.object: Run make bootstrap once; it installs the toolchain, starts the local database in Docker and seeds fixtures. Requires Docker Desktop 4.30 or newer.

facts.subject: code-review
facts.object: Pull requests over 400 changed lines should be split; every PR needs one approval from the owning team and a passing CI run.

facts.subject: performance-budget
facts.object: Largest contentful paint under 2.5 seconds and interaction to next paint under 200 milliseconds at the 75th percentile on mobile.

facts.subject: analytics-pipeline
facts.object: Events land in the warehouse through a streaming ingest with a typical delay of five minutes; dashboards are rebuilt hourly.

facts.subject: data-privacy
facts.object: Account deletion requests are completed within 30 days, including backups being aged out on the normal rotation.

facts.subject: design-system
facts.object: Spacing uses a 4 pixel base scale; colors are defined as semantic tokens, never raw hex values, so dark mode needs no component changes.

facts.subject: hiring
facts.object: Four rounds: recruiter screen, technical screen, a system design interview and a values conversation with the engineering manager.

notes.text: Spent the afternoon debugging the flaky end-to-end test in the checkout flow; the root cause was a race between the cart fetch and the coupon service mock. Fixed by awaiting the network idle state before asserting.

Architecture review for the notifications service: agreed on a queue-backed design with at-least-once delivery and a per-user digest to avoid spamming; the open question is whether to build SMS in-house.
Vendor call with the monitoring provider: the renewal quote came back 18 percent higher; asked for a multi-year discount and a clearer usage breakdown before signing.
Planning for Q4: the three bets are the payments migration, offline sync v1 and the self-serve admin console. Capacity is the constraint, so the admin console may slip to Q1.
Postmortem action items from the checkout 502: add config validation in CI, add a canary stage to config pushes, and page on error rate rather than on synthetic checks alone.
Reading group this week covered the paper on consistent hashing; the takeaway is to prefer bounded-load variants for our cache tier.
